entities.name: Janakinath Ghosal
entities.intro: Veteran Congress secretary in Calcutta who claimed a share in founding the Congress with Hume.

entities.name: Dr. P. C. Ray
entities.intro: Calcutta chemistry professor and Gokhale's neighbour. He keeps Rs. 40 of his Rs. 800 salary and gives the rest away.

entities.name: Kalicharan Banerji
entities.intro: Respected Christian Indian leader in the Congress.

entities.name: Kali temple (Kalighat)
entities.intro: Calcutta temple where animals are sacrificed to the goddess Kali.

entities.name: Swami Vivekananda
entities.intro: Famous Hindu monk based at Belur Math near Calcutta.

entities.name: Sister Nivedita
entities.intro: Irish-born disciple of Vivekananda, devoted to Hinduism.

entities.name: Burma
entities.intro: Province of British India, visited briefly by Gandhi in 1902.

entities.name: Third-class travel
entities.intro: Travelling with India's poor in third-class railway carriages.

entities.name: Benares (Kashi)
entities.intro: Holy city on the Ganges and a major Hindu pilgrimage site.

entities.name: Kevalram Mavji Dave
entities.intro: Son of Mavji Dave and a Rajkot vakil; an old well-wisher of Gandhi.

entities.name: Nature cure & hydropathy
entities.intro: Drug-free healing through diet, fasting, water and earth packs.

entities.name: Maganlal Gandhi
entities.intro: A young cousin's son whom Gandhi takes to South Africa in 1902.

entities.name: Asiatic Department
entities.intro: New Transvaal government department for 'Asiatics', staffed by officers from India and Ceylon.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has arrived for his first Indian National Congress in Calcutta, dismayed by the disorganization and dirt in the delegates' camp.
chapters.summary: To learn how the Congress works, Gandhi volunteers at its office. The veteran secretary Ghosal gives him a heap of letters to answer, and Gandhi also cheerfully buttons Ghosal's shirt for him. He meets most of the leaders, watches Gokhale and Surendranath, and notes the waste of time and the dominance of English.

updates.gandhi: Does clerical work and personal service for the Congress secretary, and learns the Congress's inner workings.
updates.ghosal: Gives Gandhi clerical work without knowing who he is. He is later embarrassed, but delighted to have Gandhi button his shirt.
updates.gokhale: Gandhi watches him at work in the Congress.
updates.incongress: Gandhi sees waste of time, overlapping work, and English dominating the proceedings.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has been doing clerical work at the Congress office; now the session itself opens and he hopes to move his South Africa resolution.
chapters.summary: The resolutions are rushed through late at night until Gokhale insists that Gandhi's South Africa resolution not be skipped. It passes unanimously in committee. In the session Gandhi has five minutes to speak, but loses his nerve and sits down when Wacha rings the warning bell. The resolution passes with everyone else's, and Gandhi is still delighted to have India's endorsement.

updates.gandhi: His South Africa resolution passes the 1901 Congress; he fumbles his five-minute speech.
updates.gokhale: Stops Pherozeshah from skipping Gandhi's resolution: 'Mr. Gandhi has been waiting long.'
updates.pherozeshah: Lets the resolution through because Gokhale has seen it.
updates.wacha: Rings the bell that makes Gandhi sit down early.
updates.incongress: Resolutions are passed in a rush, unanimously and without understanding.
updates.shyness: The facility for speaking Gandhi gained in South Africa deserts him at the Congress.

chapters.situation: The Congress is over, but Gandhi stays a month in Calcutta to lobby for South Africa's Indians, lodging at the India Club.
chapters.summary: Gokhale personally fetches Gandhi to stay with him and tells him to drop his reserve and do Congress work. At the India Club, princes who normally wear dhotis put on servants' trousers and shiny boots for Lord Curzon's durbar, and one says frankly that they are Curzon's servants. Gandhi recalls a later durbar where maharajas wore obligatory jewels, which he sees as 'insignia of their slavery'.

updates.gandhi: Moves in with Gokhale; pities India's princes as servants of the Raj.
updates.gokhale: Invites Gandhi to stay and urges him to do Congress work in India.
updates.curzon: Holds a durbar for which princes must dress as servants.
updates.malaviya: Later invites Gandhi to the durbar for the foundation of Benares Hindu University.
updates.dress: The princes' durbar costumes and jewels are 'not of their royalty, but of their slavery'.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has moved in with Gokhale in Calcutta for a month.
chapters.summary: Gokhale treats Gandhi like a younger brother and admires his self-reliance and regularity. He introduces him to Dr. P. C. Ray, who keeps Rs. 40 of his Rs. 800 salary. Gandhi sees Gokhale's single-minded devotion to India's freedom and his reverence for Ranade. Gokhale explains why a public figure needs his carriage, but Gandhi cannot get him to take walks.

updates.gandhi: Lives as Gokhale's guest and learns from watching him work.
updates.gokhale: Treats Gandhi as a brother. Devoted only to India's freedom and reveres Ranade. Defends his carriage as a necessity of public life, but takes no exercise and is often ill.
updates.pcray: Introduced by Gokhale: he keeps only Rs. 40 of his Rs. 800 salary and gives the rest to public causes.
updates.ranade: Gokhale's revered master, a judge, historian, economist and reformer; Gokhale celebrates his anniversary.
updates.simplicity: Gandhi argues with Gokhale about tramcars versus a carriage.

chapters.situation: Living with Gokhale in Calcutta, Gandhi keeps a promise to his Christian friends in South Africa to meet Indian Christians.
chapters.summary: Gandhi visits the Christian leader Kalicharan Banerji, whose wife is dying. Banerji says Christianity, unlike Hinduism, offers absolution from original sin through Jesus. Gandhi offers the Gita's path of devotion but is not satisfied. At the Kali temple he sees sheep led to sacrifice and 'rivers of blood'. He believes a lamb's life is as precious as a human's and prays for someone to end the practice.

updates.gandhi: Unconvinced by Banerji's case for Christianity. Horrified by animal sacrifice at the Kali temple and walks Calcutta's streets.
updates.kalicharan: Receives Gandhi while his wife is dying. Argues that only surrender to Jesus delivers from original sin.
updates.gokhale: Doubts Kalicharan Banerji will satisfy Gandhi, but lets him go.
updates.kalitemple: Sheep are sacrificed and the lane is lined with beggars and mendicants.
updates.christianity: A Christian Indian argues for absolution from original sin; Gandhi points to the Gita's path of devotion.
updates.ahimsa: 'The life of a lamb is no less precious than that of a human being.' Gandhi feels he needs more self-purification before he can stop such sacrifice.
updates.gita: Gandhi puts forward the Gita's path of devotion against the doctrine of original sin.

chapters.situation: Shaken by the animal sacrifices at Kalighat, Gandhi keeps exploring Bengal's religious life while lobbying for South Africa.
chapters.summary: Gandhi studies the Brahmo Samaj and attends a celebration at Devendranath Tagore's house. He walks to Belur Math but Vivekananda is ill and cannot see him. He finds little common ground with Sister Nivedita amid her splendour, though he admires her love of Hinduism. He speaks on the Boer War ambulance corps and visits Burma briefly. He then sets off on a third-class tour of India, seen off at the station by Gokhale and Dr. Ray.

updates.gandhi: Explores Bengal's religious life, visits Burma, and begins a third-class rail tour equipped with a canvas bag, blanket and Gokhale's tiffin-box.
updates.gokhale: First laughs at the third-class tour, then approves; gives Gandhi a tiffin of sweets and comes to see him off.
updates.pcray: Sees Gandhi off at the station.
updates.nivedita: Gandhi finds no common ground with her but admires her love for Hinduism.
updates.saunders: Helps Gandhi again in Calcutta despite being ill.
updates.padshah: Gandhi meets Nivedita again at Padshah's home and interprets for his mother.
updates.brahmo: Gandhi studies the Brahmo Samaj and falls in love with Bengali music.
updates.burma: Gandhi is pained by idle monks and charmed by free Burmese women, and notes Indians exploiting Burmese with English merchants.
updates.thirdclass: Gandhi's tour begins, to learn the hardships of third-class passengers.

chapters.situation: Gandhi has left Calcutta on a third-class tour across India toward Rajkot, stopping in holy cities.
chapters.summary: Gandhi finds third-class carriages filthy and overcrowded, with passengers treated like sheep, and urges educated people to travel third class to reform them. In Benares he stays with a pilgrim priest, bathes in the Ganges, and is dismayed by the noise, flies and rotting flowers at the Kashi Vishvanath temple. A priest curses him for offering one pie. He briefly pays his respects to the convalescent Annie Besant.

updates.gandhi: Spends about Rs. 31 on the whole tour. Disillusioned by the dirt and commerce of Kashi Vishvanath; offers a pie and is cursed for it.
updates.besant: Gandhi pays his respects to her in Benares as she recovers from illness.
updates.thirdclass: Third-class passengers in India are worse off than in South Africa. Gandhi calls on educated men to travel third class and reform it.
updates.benares: The temple is a noisy bazaar of flies and rotting flowers, and Gandhi 'searched here for God but failed to find Him'.
updates.religion: Gandhi sees the hypocrisy at holy places as proof of God's mercy, since the law of karma works on its own.
updates.sanitation: The holy city's temples are filthy.

chapters.situation: After his third-class tour, Gandhi must decide where in India to settle, and Gokhale wants him in Bombay.
chapters.summary: Cautious after his earlier failures, Gandhi starts in Rajkot, where Kevalram Dave gives him three briefs and he wins them all. A British judge refuses to move his court out of plague-stricken Veraval, which convinces Gandhi that Englishmen cannot think as Indians do. Kevalram insists he move to Bombay, and Gandhi takes chambers there.

updates.gandhi: Wins three cases in Kathiawad, gains confidence, and moves to Bombay with chambers at Payne, Gilbert and Sayani.
updates.kevalram: Gives Gandhi briefs, insists he not 'vegetate' in Kathiawad, and promises to send him work in Bombay.
updates.gokhale: Wants Gandhi to practise in Bombay and help with public work.
updates.law: Gandhi succeeds in Rajkot after mastering the Evidence Act, and settles in Bombay.
updates.racism: The British judge at Veraval cannot imagine Indians' hardships: 'As the elephant is powerless to think in the terms of the ant.'

chapters.situation: Gandhi has just settled in Bombay with chambers in the Fort and a house in Girgaum.
chapters.summary: Ten-year-old Manilal falls seriously ill with typhoid and pneumonia. The doctor prescribes eggs and chicken broth, but Gandhi refuses on religious grounds and treats him with Kuhne hip baths and orange juice while the doctor monitors him. With fever at 104° and delirium, Gandhi wraps him in a wet sheet pack and walks Chowpatty beach praying. He returns to find Manilal drenched in sweat, the fever breaking. Manilal recovers over 40 days on milk and fruit juice.

updates.gandhi: Refuses meat and eggs even for his gravely ill son and nurses him with hydropathy and prayer. Tormented by doubt but sure that God saved his honour.
updates.manilal: Gravely ill with typhoid at ten. Refuses eggs himself when asked, and recovers under his father's water cure to become 'the healthiest of my boys'.
updates.kasturba: Watches Manilal while Gandhi walks out to pray.
updates.naturecure: Kuhne's hip baths, fasting on orange juice, and a wet sheet pack break the fever.
updates.diet: 'Even for life itself we may not do certain things.' No meat or eggs, even in a crisis.
updates.religion: Gandhi has Ramanama on his lips and asks God to keep his honour.
updates.rambha: Ramanama, which she taught him, is his refuge in the crisis.

chapters.situation: Manilal has recovered and Gandhi's Bombay practice is going better than he expected.
chapters.summary: The family moves to a healthier bungalow in Santa Cruz. Gandhi commutes first class, gets some work, and is coached by Gokhale toward public life. Then a cable arrives: 'Chamberlain expected here. Please return immediately.' Keeping his promise, Gandhi leaves his family in Bombay and sails for South Africa with several young relatives, including Maganlal Gandhi. He reaches Durban just in time to draft the memorial for Chamberlain.

updates.gandhi: Recalled to South Africa in 1902 just as he is settling in Bombay. Leaves his family and takes enterprising young relatives with him.
updates.kasturba: Stays in the Santa Cruz bungalow with the children.
updates.maganlal: One of the young relatives Gandhi takes to South Africa, and the one Gandhi will most successfully guide to his ideals.
updates.revashankar: Helps find the Santa Cruz bungalow.
updates.gokhale: Visits Gandhi's chambers several times a week, planning his future in public life.
updates.chamberlain: Coming to South Africa, which prompts the community to recall Gandhi.
updates.truth: 'All else but God that is Truth is an uncertainty.'

chapters.situation: Gandhi has rushed back to Durban to lead an Indian deputation to the Colonial Secretary, Joseph Chamberlain, on his South African tour.
chapters.summary: Chamberlain coldly says the Empire has little control over self-governing colonies and that Indians must placate the Europeans. In the war-ravaged Transvaal, Indians now need permits from a new Asiatic Department run by officers from India and Ceylon, where touts and bribes are common. Superintendent Alexander gets Gandhi a permit in an hour, and he hurries to Pretoria.

updates.gandhi: Disappointed by Chamberlain. Gets into the Transvaal on a permit obtained through Superintendent Alexander.
updates.chamberlain: Tells the Indian deputation to placate the Europeans; Gandhi reads this as the rule that might is right.
updates.alexander: Secures Gandhi a Transvaal permit within the hour.
updates.asiaticdept: A new department created by war veterans from India and Ceylon. It turns permit-issuing into a racket with touts and bribes of up to £100.
updates.transvaal: Devastated by war; returning Indians must have permits.
updates.racism: Europeans get permits easily; Indians find it very hard.

status.gandhi: In Pretoria, preparing the Transvaal memorial

chapters.situation: Gandhi has made it to Pretoria to present the Transvaal Indians' case to Chamberlain, to the annoyance of the new Asiatic Department.
chapters.summary: The department's officials suspect Gandhi entered without a permit, then try to keep him off the deputation. Gandhi contrasts South Africa's fairly accountable officials with these 'autocrats from Asia'. The department's head, an officer from Ceylon, keeps Gandhi standing, tells him his permit was a mistake, and says he must leave and may not meet Chamberlain. He then scolds Tyeb Sheth and others to send Gandhi away.

updates.gandhi: Barred by the Asiatic Department from joining the deputation to Chamberlain and told to go back.
updates.tyeb: Defends Gandhi as 'our man' to the Asiatic chief and is scolded for it.
updates.asiaticdept: Its Ceylon-trained chief treats Indians autocratically and blocks Gandhi from seeing Chamberlain.
updates.racism: Officials bring the autocratic habits of colonial Asia to South Africa.

status.gandhi: Barred from the deputation in Pretoria
